chunks: Ibrahim ibn Hashim from an-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from Ja'far from his father from his forefathers (peace be upon them) who said:
The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) forbade the weaving of the non-Arabs (Persians) in the mosques.

key_terms.رَطَانَةِ الْأَعْجَامِ: Persian weaving/matting (a specific style of floor covering or wall decoration)

ai.seo_question: What is Ratanat al-A'jam and why was it forbidden in mosques?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the Prophet’s (peace be upon him and his family) preference for simplicity and humility in mosque furnishings, specifically discouraging the use of 'Ratanat al-A'jam' (Persian mats or woven mats), which were likely associated with luxury or foreign opulence. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on avoiding ostentation in places of worship, ensuring that the environment remains conducive to spiritual focus rather than worldly display. It reflects a broader Islamic principle of modesty in religious spaces, distinguishing between functional comfort and excessive adornment.
